headline: Copper Rebounds to $12,240 Following Brief Dip Below $12,000 Level
summary: LME three-month copper recovered 0.66% to $12,240.50 per ton after dropping briefly below $11,948. Macro nervousness over interest rates was balanced by tight physical spot market supply.
why: Copper is a vital industrial metal used in electronics, construction, and power grids, acting as a barometer for global economic health.

impacts.name: Copper
impacts.why: Tight physical inventories prompted buyers to step in after prices dropped below key psychological levels.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Physical supply deficits supported price support after an initial speculative decline.
